screen: Screened the complete active workbook for tax, tariff, fiscal and redistribution references and reviewed legal, economics, accounting and finance candidates for scope beyond word matches. Taxation in Public Economics is substantive economics. Fiscal policy in Macroeconomics, cross-border governance in International Business and trade in Business Law contribute context. The closest trial and cross-border and justice-focused variants all lack sustained application of tax legislation and procedure. Internal feasibility was tested separately to remove scheduling as an explanation for the academic outcome.

candidateAssessment.label: Comparative Law, Public Economics and Tax Policy
candidateAssessment.reason: Maastricht requires 54 EC of dedicated tax law, procedure, ethics and methods before the individual thesis. UCR offers comparative legal analysis, public economics, accounting and policy research. Public Economics examines taxation, redistribution and welfare. Constitutional and EU law teach public authority, legal remedies and free movement, and Transnational Business Law examines cross-border contracts and trade. Those contributions cover parts of the context for taxation. A feasible 24-course UCR trial still lacks a sustained sequence in applying personal, payroll, corporate and indirect tax legislation, formal tax procedure and cross-border tax rules to cases. The curricular gap remains decisive on academic grounds.

candidateAssessment.label: Cross-border Business and Tax Law
candidateAssessment.reason: EU law, international business and trade law offer a credible cross-border commercial foundation. They leave corporate tax liability, international tax allocation and tax treaty application outside the sustained coursework.

candidateAssessment.label: Tax Fairness, Public Revenue and Legal Institutions
candidateAssessment.reason: Public Economics, Ethics and policy analysis offer an economic and normative study of tax and redistribution. The available legal sequence centres general public and private law rather than fiscal procedure, taxpayers’ legal obligations or methods of interpreting tax legislation.

BENECON312.name: Econometrics
BENECON312.contribution: Builds causal and predictive modelling skills and culminates in empirical research, a distinct method from tax-law doctrine.
BENECON312.topics: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.
